h: A tall ship, a wall of cars and award-winning design
p: Moored right outside the museum is the Glenlee, a tall ship built on the Clyde in the 1890s. She sailed around the world many times and has now been beautifully restored, so you can explore the decks, the cargo hold and the crew's quarters. It's a great add-on for anyone with a love of the sea, and it gives you a sense of the shipbuilding that made Glasgow famous.

Inside, you'll find everything from old Glasgow trams and subway carriages to steam locomotives, and a huge wall of cars stacked high so you can see them from every angle. Bicycles are suspended overhead too, which makes for a fun spot of 'I had one of those' with older visitors. Shortly after it opened, the museum was named European Museum of the Year in 2013, so you're in for a treat.

Entry is free, which makes this a brilliant choice for families on a budget, and you can easily spend two to three hours here between the museum and the ship. Bring a snack for the riverside, and if the weather's good it's lovely to sit out and watch the Clyde for a while.

There's plenty more nearby. Across the river, Glasgow Science Centre at Pacific Quay is a short hop away and a must for curious kids. Upstream, the big concert arenas on the north bank bring in major acts throughout the year, and Kelvingrove Park and the West End are just a walk away along the River Kelvin.
